correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=2 and arbitrary real Hilbert target, the exact within-leaf variance identity gives R>=2-2/m and S>=2-2/n. Triangle inequality along the two leaf centroids and two centers bounds average squared cross distances below by 9 and above by the strictly variance-decreasing Phi(C), forcing the unique scalar root c. Constructing two orthogonal regular simplices and a centroid line saturates same-class, edge and across-leaf constraints; critically, opposite-center noncontraction follows from the proved c>4/(4-r) and c>4/(4-s), not from the checker. Equality of all inequalities fixes simplex Gram matrices, orthogonality, centroid order and affine rank m+n-1. Monotonicity gives balanced radicals and sharp unattained finite-size supremum. Independently rederived the inequalities and checked 20 numerical m,n cases; finite checks do not prove the infinite family.
residual_risks: At most uniqueness after normalization; all finite m,n>=2. Does not establish low fixed-dimensional embeddings.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality. The directly same-object QEC theorem computes an unsquared-distance negative-type quadratic form, not the bi-Lipschitz Hilbert distortion on original shortest-path distances. A primary exact Hilbert-distortion theorem treats complete bipartite graph metrics, not the double-star tree metric. Older general-tree distortion bounds can imply existence of a bounded embedding but not the exact two-parameter scalar root and full rigidity from their stated results. The potentially strongest 1998 source was inaccessible in full; this remains a priority risk, not a negative finding about unread content.

value.rationale: Minimum Hilbert distortion c2 is a standard geometric invariant of tree metrics; the double star is a natural diameter-three two-branch family, not an arbitrary slice. A sharp all-(m,n) formula with a monotone two-parameter law, extremal constant and complete rigidity/affine-dimension classification answers a genuine quantitative and structural question not mechanically implied by universal tree bounds.
residual_risks: Weighted variants and fixed low target dimension are not addressed; no claim of a general theory of trees.

limitations: Only unweighted double stars with at least two leaves on each side and unrestricted real Hilbert target.
